clue.text: Delivery woman, as if?

parts.note: a woman who helps at births, with the joke that the word for woman (wife) has 'if' in its middle

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off a delivery driver with a scornful 'as if'.
explanation.walkthrough: The delivery is of a baby, not a parcel. Read cryptically, the clue describes a woman (WIFE) with 'if' at her middle.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife is the trained professional who assists women in childbirth, the delivery of babies.

clue.text: Supernatural U for __, say, if polite?

parts.note: comic-alphabet joke: the missing word after 'U for' sounds like 'euphemistic', which means polite

explanation.surface: A puzzling fill-in-the-blank about what the letter U stands for when one is being courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: Comic alphabets give jokes like 'A for 'orses'. Here the blank, said after 'U for', sounds like 'euphemistic', a word meaning polite or tactful.
explanation.definitionFit: A mystic is someone in touch with spiritual or otherworldly things, so the word works as an adjective too, meaning occult.

clue.text: Foreign body or thingummy

indicators.note: something foreign is strange or altered, so these letters are made strange by rearranging them

explanation.surface: A doctor finds a foreign body, or some unnamed object, lodged somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Foreign body' looks like a medical phrase, but 'Foreign' rearranges BODY OR.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are colloquial British placeholder words for an object whose name escapes the speaker.

clue.text: Ill at home, given medicine, drinking another sip

parts.note: being in means being at home

indicators.note: something drinking takes the other piece inside it, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: dosed means given a dose of medicine

indicators.note: another version of the word sip is a rearranged form of its letters

explanation.surface: A sick patient, resting at home after medication, takes yet another sip of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' is the anagram signal: another version of SIP is ISP, which sits inside the medicine word just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Being indisposed is a mild, polite way of saying someone is unwell.

clue.text: Caesar's forty said to perform well

indicators.note: said means the letters of the Roman numeral are spoken aloud as their names

parts.note: forty in Roman numerals, the system Caesar used, is XL

explanation.surface: A remark that Julius Caesar's forty somethings performed admirably.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling out the Roman numeral XL letter by letter gives 'ex-ell'.
explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to do something outstandingly, a direct synonym for doing well.

clue.text: A flower put in shoe, medicine in it

indicators.note: put in means the river's name is placed inside the shoe's

parts.note: a mule is a backless shoe or slipper
crossword convention: a flower is something that flows, a river, here the Italian river Po

explanation.surface: Someone tucks a flower into a shoe and finds medicine inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is the usual crossword river, the Po, not a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: An ampoule is a small sealed glass vial holding a dose of liquid medicine for injection.

clue.text: Leave people under a tyre, primarily to get flat

indicators.note: in a down answer, pieces under another come after it

parts.note: to part is to leave or go away
men means people

indicators.note: primarily means the first letter of tyre is taken

explanation.surface: Motoring advice: get people out from under a tyre before it goes flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flat' looks like the state of the tyre; it is the definition, a home.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is the British word for an apartment, a set of rooms in a larger building.

clue.text: Hot in seat, how hot it is!

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for hot sits inside the word for seat

parts.note: a pew is a church seat
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone sweltering on a bench exclaims about the heat.
explanation.definitionFit: This exclamation is what people say when they are overheated, exhausted or relieved.

clue.text: Deeply fond of one's better half, you kiss and love, right? I love you so, not half!

definitions.text: Deeply fond of one's better half

parts.note: text-speak spells you as the letter U
X is the kiss at the end of a letter
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
love again is zero in tennis, O
you again as text-speak U

indicators.note: not half means only the first half of the two-letter word so is kept

explanation.surface: A doting spouse's love note: you, kisses, I love you so much.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger called this nearly an &lit: the wordplay itself is the gushing message of a devoted spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Uxorious describes a husband excessively devoted to his wife, from Latin uxor, wife.

clue.text: Attractive person caught feeding a needy sort of guy, finally

indicators.note: something feeding into another goes inside it
a sort of the words means a rearranged version of their letters
finally means the last letter of guy

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is caught feeding a needy man at the end of the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges A NEEDY into EYEAND; the cricket C slips in after its first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Eye candy is slang for someone pleasing to look at but perhaps lacking depth.

clue.text: "Sabre", "scimitar" or "steel"?

parts.note: each quoted item is a bladed weapon, and each is also a word beginning with the letter S

explanation.surface: A list of three blades, asking what they have in common.
explanation.walkthrough: Each example is a blade and also an 'S word', a word starting with S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sabre and scimitar are kinds of this blade, and steel is a poetic name for one.

clue.text: Companion: the first man, perhaps, to hug royalty

indicators.note: to hug is to wrap around, so the royal letters go inside

parts.note: a man ranked first could be called chap one
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen and so royalty

explanation.surface: Adam, the first man, perhaps embracing a royal, acting as escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the first man' suggests Adam, but it is CHAP + ONE; ER is the Queen (Elizabeth Regina).
explanation.definitionFit: A chaperone accompanies a young person to supervise them, so is a companion.

clue.text: Tories' rule hopelessly weak

indicators.note: something done hopelessly is messed up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A political jab: the Conservative government is feeble and indecisive.
explanation.walkthrough: TORIES and RULE are rearranged; the possessive apostrophe adds no letter. Tories are Britain's Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Irresolute means lacking firmness of purpose, so weak in will.

clue.text: Sporting body partial to mischief, I fancy

indicators.note: partial to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sports organisation fond of making trouble, or so one suspects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partial to' looks like 'fond of' but signals a part of the following words.
explanation.definitionFit: FIFA is the international governing organisation of football.

clue.text: Grammatical term brought up, one in decline, cut short

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the word for decline

parts.note: to abate is to decline or lessen

indicators.note: brought up in a down answer means the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a verb is a term in grammar
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson: a term is raised, one in a declension is trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses the grammar word to BREV, since down answers read upward when brought up; with I, it splits the word for decline after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abbreviate is to shorten a word or text.

clue.text: See 28
Weak lifts around a strong building, taking old, old air

indicators.note: around means the reversed word encloses the following pieces
lifts in a down answer means the word is raised, read upwards

parts.note: wet means weak or feeble
a fort is a fortified building

explanation.surface: Feeble lifts at a fortress carry old songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifts' reverses the word for weak to TEW in a down answer. 'old' appears twice on purpose: once for O, once in the definition 'old air'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tea for Two is a 1925 song from the musical No, No, Nanette, so an old tune.

clue.text: Around start of fracas, gutless frantic series of heavy blows

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
frantic means wildly disordered, so the letters are rearranged
start of means the first letter of fracas

explanation.surface: In a brawl, a cowardly person throws a frenzied flurry of punches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frantic' rearranges GUTLESS to SLUGEST, around the F of fracas.
explanation.definitionFit: A slugfest is a fight, often a boxing bout, of hard punches traded freely.

clue.text: Sustained melting catastrophic surrounding Circle

indicators.note: surrounding means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
catastrophic means ruinously disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a circle is shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: Ice melting disastrously around the Arctic Circle over a long period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catastrophic' rearranges MELTING, which then goes around O.
explanation.definitionFit: Long-time means lasting over a long period, so long-standing or sustained.

clue.text: Appear more stupid secreting drug, when cared for

indicators.note: secreting means hiding something inside

parts.note: to look is to appear
dafter means more daft, more stupid
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone looks even sillier hiding drugs while being looked after.
explanation.walkthrough: E is crossword shorthand for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To be looked after is to be cared for or tended.

clue.text: Able to get radio broadcast on time

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters of radio are rearranged

explanation.surface: Getting a radio broadcast out punctually needs skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Adroit means skilful or clever, so able.

clue.text: For example, Russian mouth organ

definitions.meaning: Russian is an example of a language
the muscular organ in the mouth used for taste and speech

explanation.walkthrough: 'mouth organ' suggests a harmonica, but it is the organ inside the mouth.
explanation.definitionFit: Tongue means a language as well as the body part in the mouth.

clue.text: Silence a lady of pop!

parts.note: to gag someone is to silence them

explanation.surface: A demand to shut a pop singer up.
explanation.walkthrough: Lady Gaga is the American pop singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is the surname part of the stage name of the pop singer Lady Gaga.

clue.text: Game taking record capital

parts.note: monte is a card game
a video is a recording

explanation.surface: A game being filmed in a big city.
explanation.definitionFit: Montevideo is the capital city of Uruguay.

clue.text: Bankers' daily crime?

definitions.meaning: the Financial Times, the daily paper read by bankers

explanation.walkthrough: The FT is the Financial Times, the British business newspaper; run together, its name is a word for stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Theft is the crime of taking someone's property dishonestly.

clue.text: Set up zero bricks

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the word is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to gel is to set, as jelly does
zero is the letter O

explanation.surface: Instructions to set up building blocks from nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses GEL to LEG.
explanation.definitionFit: Lego is the brand of plastic interlocking toy building bricks.

clue.text: Classic ballet leap — cut the chat, where's the earth moving?

parts.note: an epic is a classic work

indicators.note: cut means the following word is removed from the leap

parts.note: an entrechat is a ballet jump with beating of the legs

explanation.surface: A dancer is told to stop talking during a grand ballet leap.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing CHAT from ENTRECHAT leaves ENTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: The epicentre is the point on the surface directly above an earthquake's origin.

clue.text: In a day, beginning to grow

parts.note: Mon is the abbreviation for Monday, a day

indicators.note: beginning to means the first letter of grow

explanation.surface: Within one day, something starts to grow.
explanation.definitionFit: Among means in the midst of or surrounded by, so in.

clue.text: Lot more feverish, rapid bowing

indicators.note: feverish means agitated, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A violinist bowing faster and more frantically.
explanation.definitionFit: A tremolo on a stringed instrument is made by rapid back-and-forth bowing of one note.

clue.text: Unreal drama suggesting hater of teeth?

parts.note: a reverse anagram: the answer's last word is an anagram signal applied to its first three words, which rearranged spell out these clue words

explanation.surface: A dentist-loathing playwright writes an odd play.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: read the answer as an instruction, its last word signalling that the three words before it are an absurd rearrangement of 'hater of teeth'.
explanation.definitionFit: The theatre of the absurd is a mid-twentieth-century dramatic genre presenting illogical, unreal situations.
